newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian teachers strike, leaders still in jail.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian teachers strike, leaders still in jail.

text.p: Palestinian teachers in the West Bank town of Ramallah refused to resume work on Thursday after it transpired that strike leaders who signed an accord to end a walkout remained under Palestinian Authority detention.
Palestinian police arrested in the West Bank on Monday more than 25 teachers who were leading the strike, the first by Palestinian government employees, for higher salaries and improved conditions.
The detained strike committee was brought to Ramallah late on Wednesday for a meeting with Jibril Rajoub, head of the Palestinian Preventive Security agency in the West Bank.
Teachers said after the talks an agreement had been signed to end the strike that began in early April and that the 25 detainees had been released.
But on Thursday, teachers in Ramallah said the committee members had not been freed.

"When the committee came out of the (meeting with Rajoub), members said they were forced to sign the statement. (The Palestinian Authority) promised the teachers could go to the jail to pick up their belongings and go home, but they did not get home," Naimeh Assad, a Ramallah teacher told Reuters.
Rajoub did not return telephoned requests from Reuters for comment.
Ahmed Korei, speaker of the Palestinian Legislature, told about 400 protesters who stood outside the council demanding the teachers' freedom that he hoped a solution could be found.
"We will demand and continue working on their release," Korei told reporters in Ramallah.

About 70 percent of the 18,000 striking teachers returned to their classes in public schools in the West Bank towns of Hebron, Nablus and Jenin on Wednesday but classrooms were still closed in Ramallah.
Teachers have complained they receive about $400 a month, a sum which they say is not enough to cover their basic needs.
